newsitem.title: UK: BOE seeks comment on credit derivative supervision.
newsitem.headline: BOE seeks comment on credit derivative supervision.

text.p: The Bank of England (BOE) on Tuesday released a discussion paper on the supervision of credit derivatives and said it is seeking comments from banks on the subject.

The BOE paper set out a series of questions for comment covering all aspects of credit derivatives, from banks' existing risk management and valuation techniques to the precise treatment of credit derivatives' on banks' books.
The BOE said the paper was intended to initiate debate on the subject and was not meant as a statement of policy.
"The paper does not amend policy, but is intended to initiate debate on how best to take this issue forward," it said.
Credit derivatives consist of swap and option contracts used to assume or transfer credit risk on loans or other assets in return for interest or premium payments.
Among the issues on which the BOE seeks comment are the following:
-- do banks believe that similar risk management and valuation techniques can be applied to credit default products and total return swaps
-- how do banks manage rollover risk on total return swaps
-- how might the proposed interim treatment of total return swaps in the trading books be developed in the future
-- should total return swaps be treated in the banking book like guarantees or letters of credit.
The BOE said it was seeking comment from interested parties until January 31.
